research.facts:
Qpancy Children's Pajama Recall
**Key Facts:**
- CPSC announced recall of approximately 1,309 Qpancy children's pajama sets on Nov. 19, 2026 — HIGH
- Recall number: 27-094 — HIGH (consistent across sources)
- Hazard: Sets fail mandatory flammability requirements for children's sleepwear; pose risk of serious burn injury or death — HIGH (CPSC.gov official recall page)
- Products: Long-sleeve, button-front tops with front pocket and shorts, plus matching doll pajamas — HIGH
- Sizes: 4-5T through 10-11Y — HIGH
- Prints: Multicolor cats, pink bows and stripes — HIGH
- Sold on Amazon from March through August 2026 for approximately $20 — HIGH
- Seller: Shanghai Shengkailong Trading Co., Ltd. (doing business as Qpancy), China — HIGH
- No injuries or incidents reported — HIGH
- Consumer action: Stop use; email qpancyrecall@outlook.com for refund; cut garments in half, send photo, then discard — HIGH
- Recall page: https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2027/Qpancy-Recalls-Childrens-Pajamas-Due-to-Risk-of-Serious-Injury-or-Death-from-Burn-Hazard-Violate-Mandatory-Standards-for-Childrens-Sleepwear — HIGH
**Sources:**
- CPSC official recall — https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2027/Qpancy-Recalls-Childrens-Pajamas-Due-to-Risk-of-Serious-Injury-or-Death-from-Burn-Hazard-Violate-Mandatory-Standards-for-Childrens-Sleepwear

- AAP recommends all children 6 months and older receive 2026-27 flu vaccine as soon as it's available — HIGH (AAP official news release, Aug. 2026)

- 85% of children who died from flu last season were unvaccinated — HIGH (AAP guidance)
- As of May 2026, only 49.4% of children ages 6 months to 17 years received the flu vaccine — HIGH (AAP data)

research.facts:
Colorado Springs School Zones Expansion
**Key Facts:**
- Before 2023, school zones were largely limited to elementary schools in Colorado Springs — HIGH
- A Doherty High School student was struck and killed by a vehicle near the school in 2023, prompting the expansion — HIGH (Gazette, KOAA)
- City launched Safe Streets COS program — includes school zone enhancements, roadway/intersection improvements, trail crossing projects, and partnerships with CSPD on speed safety cameras — HIGH (coloradosprings.gov)
- New zones being added to multiple middle and high schools: Vista Ridge, Sierra, Cheyenne Mountain, Mann, Panorama, West, Palmer High School among others — MEDIUM (Gazette Feb. 2026 report; some may not be complete yet)
- Flashers at Sierra High School operational for 2026-27 school year — MEDIUM
- Installation at Panorama Middle School set for completion "by end of summer" — MEDIUM (timing may have passed; treat as "recently completed")
- New zones affect D11, D20, and D49 schools — HIGH
- State bill HB26-1318 "Traffic Safety Near Schools" heard by legislature in 2026 — MEDIUM (outcome unknown)
**Sources:**
- Gazette: "Colorado Springs increasing safety around more schools in 2026" — https://gazette.com/?p=1537953
- KOAA: "School zones coming to several middle and high schools across Colorado Springs" — https://www.koaa.com/news/covering-colorado/school-zones-coming-to-several-middle-and-high-schools-across-colorado-springs

research.facts:
D11 Enrollment Update — Underused Campuses
**Key Facts:**
- D11 presented enrollment and capacity updates at a Nov. 18, 2026 work session — HIGH (KRDO.com)
- 11 D11 schools meet state criteria for being "underused" — HIGH (KRDO.com)
- Despite multiple underused campuses, D11 says it has NOT seen enrollment declines and is NOT planning school closures — HIGH (KRDO)
- District said it increased enrollment overall and is not closing schools — HIGH
- D11 is pursuing "co-location" — sharing a building among more than one school or program — HIGH
- District acknowledged need to "communicate earlier and more often with school communities" on co-locations — HIGH (KRDO)
- D11 $775M bond approved Nov. 2026 election (Ballot Issue 4A) — HIGH (covered Nov. 24 pipeline)
- Independent citizen oversight committee proposed to monitor bond spending — HIGH (covered Nov. 24 pipeline)
- D49 is now the largest school district in El Paso County, surpassing D11 — HIGH (Gazette 2025 state enrollment data)
**Sources:**
- KRDO: "Colorado Springs School District 11 reports 11 underused campuses, shares capacity updates ahead of 2026-27 school year" (Nov. 19, 2026) — https://krdo.com/news/2026/11/19/d11-enrollment-school-capacity/
